text: Which sub-regions should a territory split into?

options.label: 1936 provinces, with scenario overrides: Baleares as its three islands, Asturias in 2, Madrid in 3 (about 55 sub-regions)
options.rationale: Historical borders straight from the data, and the overrides cover the two contested territories and Madrid that provinces alone cannot split.

options.label: Pure 1936 provinces (48; Asturias, Baleares and Madrid never split)
NUTS3 as published (52; Baleares splits, Asturias and Madrid never split)
Fewer merged zones, at most 5 per territory as plan.md section 9.2 says (about 35)
Drop this idea or defer it

text: Should armies move between sub-regions, or should sub-regions only decide control and income?

options.label: Hybrid: orders and battles stay on the 18 territories; sub-regions decide control, cities, income and supply
options.rationale: Gives the contested-front and income effect at about a third of the cost, and keeps the data ready for full sub-region movement later.

options.label: Full sub-region movement now, every army on one of about 55 sub-regions (needs idea 6 multi-step movement)
Sub-regions only while a territory is split; unified territories move as today

text: When a graded battle result says k sub-regions change hands, which ones go?

options.label: Automatic: the defender's sub-regions bordering the attack's origin, taking the one with the most attacker-held neighbours each time; ties by scenario order
options.rationale: Deterministic, explainable in one line, and grows a contiguous front from the side the attack came from.

options.label: The attacker names target sub-regions in its order, in priority order
Seeded random choice among the bordering sub-regions

text: How do two factions fight inside a partitioned territory?

options.label: An explicit Push order (a move order to its own territory) attacks the enemy zone; otherwise armies dig in and the front holds
options.rationale: Stable, holdable fronts are what partitioning is for; today's automatic M27 battle every turn would grind every split territory.

options.label: Keep M27 automatic standing battles every turn, with the graded result moving sub-regions
Both: automatic battles unless both sides entrench

text: How does a partitioned territory count toward the territory victory share?

options.label: It counts for nobody until one faction holds every sub-region (as contested territories do today)
options.rationale: No change to M10 or the victory thresholds, and it rewards finishing a territory.

options.label: It counts for the faction holding most of its sub-regions
Victory counts sub-regions instead of territories (new thresholds needed)

text: Where do defenders go when the sub-region they stood in is taken?

options.label: They fall back into the nearest sub-region of the same territory their faction still holds; if none, they retreat under M21
options.rationale: Keeps the territory contested instead of emptying it, which is the point of a partial result.

options.label: They always retreat out of the territory under M21
Armies in a lost sub-region are destroyed

text: How should the Spain scenario start on 31 July 1936?

options.label: Already partitioned: each sub-region goes to the holder of its provincial capital, with hand overrides where that misleads (Aragon's Republican east); for example Andalucia 5 Southern, 3 Republic
options.rationale: Close to the 1936 map and turns contested flags into real fronts; the capital rule alone would hand all of Aragon to the Northern command.

options.label: Keep today's contested flags and let the first battles create the splits
Partitioned, but with each sub-region assigned by researched countryside control rather than its capital

text: When an army moves into a partitioned territory where its own faction already has a zone, does it fight?

options.label: It attacks if an enemy sub-region borders the territory it came from; otherwise it joins its own zone as a reinforcement
options.rationale: The front you meet is the one facing your approach, and the attack's origin then feeds the split rule; today's M11 would make every such move a non-fighting reinforcement.

options.label: It always joins its own zone; only a Push order from inside fights
The player chooses: reinforce the zone or attack the enemy zone

text: How should rail move armies?

options.label: Lines with a level (0 to 3) that sets per-line capacity (armies per turn) and range; the weakest segment caps a route
options.rationale: Shows the bottleneck the owner asked for (Madrid-Valencia) and makes junction cities worth taking.

options.label: One rail-point pool per faction per turn, as in Paths of Glory strategic redeployment; lines only gate where
Rail carries supply only, not armies (HOI4 style)
Drop this idea or defer it

text: Can an army arrive by rail into a battle?

options.label: No: rail moves only into ground its faction controls with no enemy army, like an M11 reinforcement
options.rationale: Matches the history (rail redeployed reserves, trucks led assaults) and Paths of Glory, and keeps validation on the start-of-turn state.

options.label: Yes: the last step may attack, at a penalty
Yes, with no penalty

text: Can players build and upgrade rail?

options.label: Build and upgrade one level at a time, paying Funds over several turns, on a connection whose both ends you hold
options.rationale: The owner asked for it, 18xx shows one-step upgrades read well, and the 1938 Torrejon-Tarancon line shows building took many turns.

options.label: Upgrade existing 1936 lines only; no new lines
Fixed 1936 network; no building

text: What happens to a line when its end changes hands?

options.label: It drops one level (demolition) and the new holder can repair it
options.rationale: Gives rail a front-line cost without tracking rolling stock, and gives building orders a use.

options.label: Nothing; the new holder uses it at once
It is destroyed and must be rebuilt

text: Should the engine model track gauge now?

options.label: No; add an optional gauge field later, for a WW1 or WW2 scenario
options.rationale: Spain's main network was one broad gauge; the only break was at the French border, which only matters for foreign aid.

options.label: Yes: an optional gauge per line, plus transshipment cost at a break

text: Should rail affect supply in Milestone 3?

options.label: No; supply traces through controlled ground only, and rail-borne supply waits for Milestone 4
options.rationale: Keeps both new systems small and separately testable.

options.label: Yes: supply traced beyond N steps must use rail

text: Where do armies stand relative to cities?

options.label: In the territory (in their faction's zone under idea 7); drop cityId from units; a city is a feature of its sub-region
options.rationale: Exactly the owner's request, and cityId is display-only today, so no rule is lost.

options.label: Keep cityId as display placement only (status quo)
A city is a separate garrison point armies can enter and be besieged in

text: Which city buildings should Milestone 3 offer? Choose all that apply.

options.label: Depot, Workshop, Fortifications, Port
options.rationale: Each one maps onto a system Milestone 3 already has or adds: recruitment, Funds, works, and sea moves.

options.label: Airfield (only if idea 8 adds aircraft)
Rail yard (only if idea 5 lands)
Hospital (faster replenishment)
Drop this idea or defer it

text: How do builds work?

options.label: One build at a time per city, paid at reveal, finished after its turns, refunded if the city is lost first
options.rationale: Same hidden-order pipeline as recruitment, one queue slot per city, and nothing to micromanage.

options.label: Builds finish instantly
Several builds at once per city

text: What happens to buildings when a city is captured?

options.label: Captured, one level down
options.rationale: Makes cities prizes without letting a raid erase a turn's investment entirely.

options.label: Captured intact
Destroyed

text: Should besieged cities (Oviedo, the Toledo Alcazar) get a rule of their own?

options.label: No new rule: a city's sub-region gives its defender +1, and a surrounded city is cut off from supply (mismatch c)
options.rationale: Most of a siege falls out of sub-regions plus supply; a separate siege battle type is a second combat system.

options.label: Yes: a Here I Stand-style siege where a city keeps its holder until a successful assault
Drop this idea or defer it

text: Should sea connections require a controlled port at each end?

options.label: Yes, with a balance check: test it against the Southern command's 13 percent win share before shipping
options.rationale: It fixes D32 (the whole Army of Africa crossing on turn 1) historically, but Malaga being Republican would block Melilla's crossing.

options.label: Yes, unconditionally
No; sea moves stay ordinary moves (status quo)

text: Does Milestone 3 need supply at all?

options.label: Smallest version: trace through own ground (and own ports by sea) to a scenario-tagged source city; affects income and recruitment only
options.rationale: Covers all three uses in the old draft with one breadth-first search a turn, and models besieged cities.

options.label: Drop the word: income and recruitment need control only
Full supply with combat penalties and attrition

text: Which cities are supply sources?

options.label: Scenario-tagged list (for Spain: major ports, rail hubs, and Ceuta and Melilla)
options.rationale: Data, not code; lets the cut-off Republican north stay supplied through Bilbao and Gijon.

options.label: Every controlled city
Only each faction's capital
